meta.probingQuestion: How do you use your strength without taking someone else's?

games.title: Half Guard with Standing Transition Game

meta.connection: You can have full control of someone's back and still choose not to hurt them. That is the whole system: the power to hurt, and the choice not to. Using your strength for people instead of over them is that same choice, made in your life.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, half guard, and back control. You can control someone's back and still choose not to hurt him. That is the point. Using strength for people, not over them, is the same choice off the mat. You get to hold power and choose mercy.

slides.title: How do you use your strength without taking someone else's?

body.text: This is tripping him by blocking his foot.

items: The overhook player wins when the underhook player falls onto his own hips or hands.
The underhook player wins by closing his own hands under the overhook player's elbows.

body.text: This is getting close to someone lying down.

items: The bottom player wins by getting his feet inside and sitting up, or, once the top player stands, by wrapping both legs around one of his legs.
The top player wins by locking his hands around the bottom player.

body.text: This is holding his back from behind.

items: The top player holds as long as his chest stays on the bottom player's back.
The bottom player wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Tonight you had full control of his back. What kept him safe?

options.text: Keeping your chest on him, not squeezing.
Squeezing him as hard as you can.
options.feedback: Squeezing takes his strength instead of using yours.

options.text: Wrapping your legs around his waist.
options.feedback: Your legs aren't what kept him safe.

slides.bridge: Strength used for control keeps him safe instead of taking from him.
